```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A plan change rarely moves one thing. Exampleton's Plan Change 1 raises a
height limit, creates a zone, rezones the blocks near the station, maps a
wider flood plain and re-subdivides a block, all at once. This vignette
compares it with the operative plan: what changed, where, and why.

```{r setup}
library(plancap)
```

## Two scenarios

A **scenario** is everything that determines capacity. A plan change is
written as a change from the baseline, naming only what differs:

```{r}
town <- exampleton()
pc1 <- exampleton_pc1()
base <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
                 parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ],
                 roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
                 zoning = town$zoning,
                 layers = town[c("height_areas", "flood_hazard", "heritage", "trees",
                                 "precincts", "transit")],
                 water = town$water, centrelines = town$road_centrelines)
change <- scenario_change(base, "PC1 as notified",
                          rulebook = pc1$rulebook,
                          zoning = pc1$zoning,
                          layers = list(flood_hazard = pc1$flood_hazard),
                          parcels = pc1$parcels[pc1$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ])
set <- scenario_set(base, change)
set
```

The PC1 rulebook is a file that `extends:` the operative one and states
only its changes:

```{r, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(readLines(rulebook_example_path("exampleton_pc1"))[-(1:9)], sep = "\n")
```

The same set can be written as a manifest file and read with
`read_scenarios()`; the one for this example ships with the package:

```{r}
identical(names(read_scenarios(system.file("extdata", "exampleton_pc1_scenarios.yaml",
                                           package = "plancap"))),
          c("Operative", "PC1 as notified"))
```

## What changed in the inputs

```{r}
diff_inputs(base, change)
```

## Running and comparing

`run_scenarios()` runs the baseline in full and the change incrementally:
only sites whose inputs differ are rebuilt.

```{r}
res <- run_scenarios(set)
cmp <- compare_scenarios(res)
cmp
```

## Why: the drivers

The change is split into its drivers by running intermediate scenarios that
switch one driver at a time, in order (rules, then zoning, then overlay
layers, then parcels). The drivers add exactly to the total change, and the
rules driver splits further by the zones and overlays whose rules changed:

```{r}
p <- cmp$pairs[[1]]
p$attribution
p$rule_attribution
```

Here PC1's new MDR height adds floor area on every MDR site; the rezoning
to Terraced Housing adds more; the wider flood plain takes some away; the
re-subdivided block changes little. `attribution = "shapley"` averages
over every order instead, at the cost of more runs. (With this plan change
it warns: some orders apply the new zoning before the new rules, so land is
zoned to a zone the old rulebook does not have.)

## Where: zones, sites and areas

Zone transitions show land and capacity moving from each operative zone to
each PC1 zone:

```{r}
tr <- p$transitions
tr[tr$land_area > 1 & tr$from != tr$to, c("from", "to", "land_area", "floor_area_change", "dwellings_change")]
```

Every baseline site carries its change and a reason:

```{r}
table(p$sites$reason)
head(sf::st_drop_geometry(p$sites)[p$sites$reason == "rezoned",
                                   c("unit", "zone_baseline", "zone_scenario", "floor_area_change")])
```

Where the parcels changed (the re-subdivided block), the new lots' capacity
is apportioned to the old parcels by area, so the change still has a place.
A common geography (`areas = ` or `grid = `) is always comparable:

```{r}
cmp_grid <- compare_scenarios(res, grid = 400, attribution = "none")
g <- cmp_grid$pairs[[1]]$by_grid
g[order(-g$floor_area_change), c("grid", "floor_area_baseline", "floor_area_scenario", "floor_area_change")][1:5, ]
```

## Checking it adds up

```{r}
check_comparison(cmp)
```
